chunks: Say: 'Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls the hearing and the eyes? And who brings forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living? And who directs all affairs?' They will say: 'God.' So tell them: 'Why do you not fear Him?'

key_terms.يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ: brings forth the living from the dead

ai.seo_question: What are the key divine attributes mentioned in Surah Yunus verse 31 that prove God's oneness?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to demonstrate the unity of divine attributes, linking Allah's role as the Provider (Ar-Razzaq) directly to His sovereignty over life, death, and cosmic administration (Al-Tadbir). The rhetorical question anticipates the polytheists' acknowledgment of God's power, using their own confession to urge them toward Taqwa, thereby establishing a logical bridge between intellectual recognition of Tawhid and practical spiritual mindfulness.
